services.name: Water damage restoration
services.summary: Burst pipes, appliance leaks, and flooding. We extract the water, dry the structure, and prove it's dry before anything gets closed up.
now: Shut off the main water valve if the source is a pipe or appliance.
Turn off power to wet rooms at the breaker if it's safe to reach.
Move furniture, rugs, and electronics off wet floors.
Photograph everything before you clean up.
steps: We find every wet area with moisture meters and thermal imaging, including inside walls and under flooring.
Truck-mounted and portable extractors pull standing water out of floors and carpet.
Dehumidifiers and air movers run while we take daily readings until materials reach dry standard.
Photos, moisture logs, and a written scope for your insurance claim.
faqs: How long does drying take?
Most structures dry in 3 to 5 days. Hardwood, plaster, and saturated subfloors can take longer; daily readings tell us when it's done.
Does homeowners insurance cover water damage?
Sudden and accidental leaks are usually covered. Gradual leaks and outside flooding often aren't. Your policy decides, and we document the loss either way.
Do I need to move out?
Usually not. If the kitchen, only bathroom, or electrical is affected, your policy may pay for temporary housing.

services.name: Fire and smoke damage restoration
services.summary: Soot, smoke odor, and water from firefighting. We secure the property, clean or remove what's damaged, and get rid of the smell for good.
now: Stay out until the fire department says the building is safe.
Don't wipe soot; it smears and sets into surfaces.
Don't turn on the HVAC; it spreads soot through the ducts.
Call your insurer to open a claim.
steps: Board-up and roof tarping keep weather and intruders out.
Dry sponging, HEPA vacuuming, and surface-specific cleaners for walls, ceilings, and contents.
Thermal fogging, hydroxyl, or ozone treatment, depending on the materials.
Repair or rebuild damaged areas, or hand off to our reconstruction crew.
faqs: Can smoke smell really be removed?
Yes, when the source residue is cleaned and the odor is neutralized rather than masked. Porous items that can't be cleaned are documented for replacement.
What about wildfire smoke?
Smoke from nearby wildfires gets into attics, HVAC, and soft goods even without flames. It's cleaned the same way and is often covered.

services.name: Mold remediation
services.summary: Visible growth or a musty smell. We contain the area, remove the mold, fix the moisture source, and clear the space for a post-test.
now: Don't touch, scrub, or bleach it; that releases spores.
Keep the door to the affected room closed.
Stop the moisture source if you can find it.
Keep anyone with asthma or allergies away from the area.
steps: Find the extent of growth and the moisture that's feeding it.
Plastic barriers and negative air pressure keep spores from spreading through the house.
Affected drywall, insulation, and materials come out; framing is cleaned and treated.
An independent post-remediation test confirms the area is clear.
faqs: Do I need a mold test first?
If growth is visible, testing isn't required to start. Testing helps when you smell mold but can't see it, and after remediation to confirm it's gone.
Is mold covered by insurance?
Mold from a covered water loss often is, up to a policy limit. Mold from long-term humidity usually isn't.

services.name: Sewage cleanup
services.summary: Toilet overflows and sewer backups. Category 3 water needs protective equipment, removal of porous materials, and disinfection.
now: Keep people and pets away from the area.
Stop using toilets, sinks, and drains in the house.
Don't run fans; they spread contaminants.
Wash hands right away after any contact.
steps: Crews in protective equipment set up containment.
Contaminated water and porous materials such as carpet, pad, and drywall come out.
Hard surfaces are cleaned and treated with antimicrobials.
The area is dried and rebuilt once it's clean.
faqs: Can carpet be saved after a sewage backup?
No. Carpet and pad touched by sewage are removed. Hard surfaces can be cleaned and disinfected.
Who pays for a sewer backup?
Many policies exclude it unless you have a sewer backup endorsement. If the city main caused it, a claim with the city may apply.

services.name: Storm damage repair
services.summary: Wind, rain, and fallen trees. We tarp the roof, board openings, dry what got wet, and start the repairs.
now: Stay clear of downed power lines and report them to PG&E.
Move valuables away from leaks and put buckets under drips.
Photograph the outside and inside damage.
Don't climb on the roof.
steps: Emergency roof tarping and board-up stop more water from getting in.
Water that came through the roof or walls is removed and the structure is dried.
Photos and a written scope for your claim.
faqs: How fast can you tarp a roof?
Tarping is first priority on a storm call because it prevents additional damage, and most policies require you to take reasonable steps to stop it.

services.name: Reconstruction
services.summary: After the cleanup, the rebuild. Drywall, flooring, cabinets, and paint, so the same company finishes the job it started.
steps: A line-item estimate that matches what your insurer approved.
Drywall, texture, paint, flooring, cabinets, and trim.
We walk the finished work with you before we close out.
faqs: Can I use my own contractor for the rebuild?
Yes. You choose who rebuilds. We can hand off the documentation, or finish the job ourselves so there's one point of contact.
